body:
## Problem — code

`merge._merge_one` relies on `gh pr merge` to fail closed ("a failing required check"). That only covers checks the host repo marks **required** in branch protection. A host whose protection is thin lets a wave PR auto-merge while its real gates are red or still running: getwyrd/wyrd's `main` currently requires only `docs-check` / `require-issue` / `docs-immutability` — a red `rust`/`gate` or an unfinished CodeQL run would not stop the merge. The harness's correctness shouldn't hinge on every instance operator having configured branch protection tightly.

## Proposal — code

Before `gh pr ready`/`gh pr merge`, read the PR's full check rollup (`gh pr checks --json name,bucket` or the status API) and refuse to merge unless every check is green (pending included — waiting or STOP, not merging past an in-flight run). Same fail-closed STOP style as the existing paths. An opt-out knob (`merge_requires = "all" | "required"`) if someone genuinely wants host-config semantics.

## Problem — docs

`template/docs/fork-discipline.md.jinja` §2 states flatly: the automation "never marks a PR ready and never merges." `wave_mode = "merge"` — the harness's own opt-in — does both for non-final waves (`merge.py`, since #279). The template contradicts the feature; instances that enable merge mode inherit a discipline doc that no longer describes their system.

## Proposal — docs

Scope the claim in the template the way the instance-side fix did (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#198, INTEGRATION.md "Ready-mark gate"): the never-ready/never-merge rule binds the **model leaves** unconditionally and every **final-wave** PR; under `wave_mode = "merge"` the deterministic driver readies+merges non-final waves at the boundary, with per-bundle human sign-off before publish and the (fixed, per above) check-rollup gate as the guardrails.
title: merge mode: gate the auto-merge on the PR's full check rollup, not the host's required-checks config; scope fork-discipline.md's never-merges claim
